correctness.rationale: The algebraic identities A^nC=D_{n+1}-D_nB and CB^n=D_{n+1}-AD_n are exact. Normal-extension interpolation gives AC and CB in S_{np}; the two hyponormal range inequalities give A*C and CB* in the same class. The identity CC*C=CX*A*C-CB*X*C then puts CC*C in S_{np}, and polar decomposition converts this exactly to C in S_{3np}. The root-of-unity diagonal example checks the lower barrier without complementability or inheritance assumptions.

originality.rationale: Kittaneh 1986 gives S_{8p} for powers 2 and 3, while Kittaneh 2006 gives S_{2^{n+1}p} for consecutive powers under range inclusion. Duggal 2001 treats coprime powers under different additional hypotheses, and Bhatia-Kittaneh 1997 gives stronger conclusions in special self-adjoint or positive settings. No equivalent linear-in-n exponent for the general subnormal consecutive-power case was located. Residual risk from older ideal and subnormal-operator literature remains.

value.rationale: The result changes the known dependence on the power index from exponential to linear and supplies an explicit linear-order obstruction, locating the optimal universal exponent between (n+1)p and 3np. The same cubic observation also improves the arbitrary-ideal root exponent under the older weaker hypotheses.
